questions.question: What was the radio-flux advantage of VIPS relative to MOJAVE and similar samples for studying EGRET blazars?

options.A: Its flux limit was roughly an order of magnitude lower
options.B: Its flux limit was roughly an order of magnitude higher
options.C: It observed only the brightest 12 EGRET sources at 15 GHz
options.D: It used a gamma-ray rather than radio flux selection

questions.rationale: The authors emphasize VIPS reaches substantially fainter radio flux densities than the comparison surveys.
questions.evidence_quote: VIPS has a ﬂux limit roughly an order of magnitude below the MOJAVE survey

questions.question: How did the authors define the EGRET-candidate VIPS subset and its confidence categories?

options.A: Intersecting EGRET with CRATES at |b|>10°, then labeling candidates by FoM thresholds >1 and 0.25–1
options.B: Selecting all VIPS sources within 10° of the Galactic plane, using radio flux alone
options.C: Cross-matching EGRET with MOJAVE and dividing at a 15 GHz spectral-index threshold
options.D: Selecting sources detected in both EGRET and VIPS, then labeling by redshift completeness

questions.rationale: The candidate set came from EGRET×CRATES and FoM combines radio, spectral, X-ray, and positional information.
questions.evidence_quote: A source is considered “likely” if it has FoM > 1, and “plausible” if it has 1.0 > FoM > 0.25.

questions.question: What does the reported 31-source EGRET-candidate morphology census include after adding MOJAVE objects?

options.A: 8 point sources, 4 short jets, and 19 long jets
options.B: 8 point sources, 3 short jets, and 14 long jets
options.C: 12 point sources, 4 short jets, and 15 long jets
options.D: 8 point sources, 7 short jets, and 13 long jets

questions.rationale: The VIPS-only counts are 8 PS, 3 SJET, 14 LJET; adding six MOJAVE sources yields totals 8, 4, and 19.
questions.evidence_quote: adds 5 LJET and 1 SJET for totals of 8 (25%) PS, 4 (13%) SJET, and 19 (61%) LJET.

questions.question: Compared with the VIPS population, which morphology imbalances among EGRET candidates were reported as marginally significant?

options.A: A deficit of compact symmetric objects and an excess of long-jet sources
options.B: An excess of point sources and a deficit of short-jet sources
options.C: A deficit of long-jet sources and an excess of complex sources
options.D: An excess of compact symmetric objects and a deficit of point sources

questions.rationale: The text calls the CSO shortage and LJET excess marginally significant, while PS and SJET counts are roughly as expected.
questions.evidence_quote: a marginally signiﬁcant lack of CSOs, and a marginally signiﬁcant excess of sources with long jets

questions.question: What were the polarization detection fraction and comparison fraction for the EGRET candidates, and what caveat did the authors stress?

options.A: 48±12% versus 36±4% overall VIPS; small samples and mixed 5/15 GHz measurements limit inference
options.B: 36±4% versus 48±12% overall VIPS; identical-frequency sampling makes the difference definitive
options.C: 61±13% versus 41±4% among LJETs; the distributions were statistically conclusive
options.D: 48±4% versus 36±12% among MOJAVE; all measurements were at 5 GHz

questions.rationale: The combined sample yields 48±12% polarization detection against 36±4% VIPS overall, but the number statistics and mixed frequencies impede a firm conclusion.
questions.evidence_quote: This is higher than the average of 36 ± 4% in VIPS overall

questions.question: What was the K-S test probability for the EGRET and overall VIPS core-to-jet ratio distributions being drawn from the same parent population?
questions.rationale: The authors interpret the histograms as showing more core-dominated EGRET objects and report a 4% same-parent probability.
questions.evidence_quote: The K-S test probability that the two distributions were drawn from the same parent distribution is 4%.

questions.question: How did the authors estimate brightness temperatures for compact cores whose fitted size was below the minimum observable size?

options.A: They substituted the minimum resolvable size, about 10% of VIPS sources, yielding a lower limit on core TB
options.B: They set the size to zero and reported an exact infinite TB
options.C: They used the brightest jet component's size for every unresolved core
options.D: They applied a rest-frame redshift correction and discarded unresolved objects

questions.rationale: For estimated core sizes below the visibility-based minimum, the minimum size was used; resulting TB values are indicated as lower limits.
questions.evidence_quote: we used the minimum size to compute TB.

questions.question: How was each jet opening half-angle ψ constructed from the fitted component geometry?

options.A: arctan[(|y′|+dr)/|x′|], with dr the deconvolved Gaussian size perpendicular to the jet axis
options.B: arctan[(|x′|+dr)/|y′|], with dr the restoring beam FWHM along the jet
options.C: The mean position angle of the outermost components divided by their radial separation
options.D: The deconvolved core diameter divided by the total projected jet length

questions.rationale: The paper defines rotated offsets relative to the axis and adds deconvolved transverse extent before taking the arctangent.

questions.question: How strong was the evidence for an EGRET/VIPS jet-length difference from the full VIPS sample?

options.A: There was no appreciable difference; the K-S same-distribution probability was 34%
options.B: EGRET jets were significantly longer; the probability was 4%
options.C: EGRET jets were significantly shorter; the probability was 11%
options.D: There was no difference because all sources had identical rest-frame lengths

questions.rationale: Despite a slight excess of long-jet morphologies, the jet-length distributions showed no appreciable difference and a 34% K-S probability.
questions.evidence_quote: The K-S probability that the two are drawn from the same distribution is 34%.

questions.question: What interpretation unifies the higher core fractions, core brightness temperatures, polarization, and apparent motions of gamma-ray-loud blazars in the paper?

options.A: A higher mean Doppler factor from smaller viewing angles and tighter gamma-ray beaming
options.B: A systematically lower intrinsic radio luminosity that makes jets appear more compact
options.C: A larger redshift distribution that raises observed brightness temperatures
options.D: A lower jet speed that reduces projection effects and increases core fraction

questions.rationale: The authors connect the observed properties to gamma-ray-selected jets oriented closer to the line of sight and higher Doppler factors.
questions.evidence_quote: gamma-ray selected sources have higher Doppler factors than the population of compact sources as a whole.
